pages.lesson:
LESSON: WRITING 4.3.1 WRITING TO GIVE INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.3: Writing 4.3.1 Writing to give information

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Writing 4.3.1 Writing to give information. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why is it important to understand how to respond to an emergency?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. write a composition on the process of responding to an emergency in school

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Writing 4.3.1 Writing to give information makes your writing clear so others can read it easily.

• Look at the model your teacher shows. Notice shape, order, and spacing.

• Practise slowly first, then build neat speed.

• Check your work: Did you spell carefully? Did you use correct marks?

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Copy three model sentences neatly, leaving finger spaces between words.

Example 2: Spell five lesson words aloud, then write them without looking.

Example 3: Fix this sentence by adding capital letters and a full stop: “amina went to kisumu”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Write five neat sentences about your school using words from this topic.
2. Exchange books with a friend and check spelling or punctuation together.
3. Rewrite one messy sentence so it is clear and correct.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Complete a short guided paragraph in your exercise book.
2. List eight words from this topic and practise spelling them with a parent.
3. Write a short note to a friend using correct punctuation.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Watch a short video or read a passage on the process of responding to an emergency,
2. Compile a list of connectors of sequence used to sequence ideas in paragraphs (e.g. first, second, then, finally),
3. Write a composition laying out the process of responding to an emergency based on the main steps outlined using the connectors of sequence,
4. Digital Literacy: The learner interacts with digital content to watch a short video or read a passage on the process of responding to an emergency.
5. Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: This is enhanced as the learner analyses concepts logically to outline the main steps taken in responding to the emergency in the video or passage. Values:

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Neat writing helps the reader.
2. Check spelling and punctuation before you finish.
3. Practice a little every day.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
